title: Google launches AI voice features in Gmail, Docs, and Keep
slides: Can Google's voice weave into your workflow?
Gmail, Docs, and Keep now hear your commands.
But voice input remains silent in offline mode.
Typing speed no longer decides your email response time.
Try voice dictation for one message today.
thread_text:
1. Your typing speed just became obsolete.

Google now lets you dictate in Gmail, Docs, and Keep — no more waiting for your fingers to catch up with your thoughts.

2. But there's a catch — no offline voice.

If you're on a plane or in a dead zone, your voice commands disappear. You're back to typing, not talking.

3. Email replies just got faster.

Voice dictation turns a 3-minute response into a 10-second one. But can it handle your jargon and slang?

4. Does accuracy beat speed?

You'll save time composing, but you'll still need to proofread every word. A misheard name could cost you a client.

5. Try it on one email today.

Open Gmail, hit the mic, and dictate a reply. Does the time saved justify the edits? Test it now.
video_script: Typing is dead. Google adds voice.

script: Typing is dead. Google adds voice.

instagram.caption:
Your fingers just became optional inside Google’s core apps.

Gmail, Docs, and Keep now take voice dictation directly. You speak, they type—no third-party tool needed.

One limit: this vanishes offline. On a plane or in a tunnel, the mic goes silent, and you’re back to manual typing.

For anyone drafting content or replies, this cuts a 3-minute reply to about 10 seconds. But you’ll still need to eyeball every sentence before hitting send—misheard names and jargon slip through silently.

Open Gmail, tap the mic on one draft, and dictate a full reply. Did you catch an error in the first 10 seconds? 🎤
